summary: Plan v04 scoped Phases 4-7 (bi-lasso completeness front); Phases 1-2 preserved, Phase 3/8 deferred to a separate soundness research task per the plan's own re-scope decision (not a partial outcome by itself). This dispatch: Phase 4 landed its tractable sub-items zero-debt and verified (4a's conversion half -- instantStrict_constraint_lt -- and 4b in full -- periodicReducePast + property lemma, extractModelZPeriodicPast + 3 property lemmas). Phase 4c/4d (wiring the periodic model in as the real extractModelZ) hit a genuine structural gap: tracing isTemporalClosed/findEventualityDefect/findBlockedTime/isSubsetBlocked against temporalStepBranch/processNext found that (a) genuinely-saturated open branches always have an empty eventuality tracker (island model already suffices, no periodic construction needed), and (b) fuel-exhausted open branches -- the only case that DOES need the periodic construction -- may carry no isSubsetBlocked witness at all among their own labels, requiring an unformalized fuel-sufficiency/pigeonhole theorem to rule out. blockers.description: Phase 4c/4d cannot generically derive a loop witness (t_anc, t_new) satisfying isSubsetBlocked from an arbitrary temporalTableau openBranch result. Genuinely-saturated open branches always have empty pending trackers (no periodic model needed); fuel-exhausted open branches (the case that DOES need it) may have no internal isSubsetBlocked witness at all, requiring an unformalized fuel-sufficiency/pigeonhole theorem (temporalFuel's 2^n-distinct-time-types bound guarantees blocking triggers before fuel exhausts) that is not yet present anywhere in the codebase. Secondary finding: temporalStepBranch's .branching arm passes EventualityTracker through unchanged, so untlPos/sncePos's primary recurring copy is never registered as pending by that call site either. Full trace in Completeness.lean module docstring ('Blocked (FMP Existence Argument)') and the plan file's Phase 4 BLOCKER writeup.

dead_ends: Deriving isSubsetBlocked existence generically from ancestorTimes (Branch.lean) membership: ancestorTimes is a bidirectional (predecessor+successor) transitive closure over ord.constraints, so t_anc in ancestorTimes ord t carries no guaranteed direction/order relative to t -- InstantStrict alone cannot convert an arbitrary ancestorTimes membership into a strict hL without also knowing which direction the traversal took.

Assuming genuine saturation (temporalStepBranch = none) can occur with nonempty pending eventualities: ruled out, since a live Until/Since branching copy would still be expandable, so full saturation forces an empty tracker (the periodic construction is not needed there at all).
